record.original_question: Study the geometry of the variety of uniform (translation-invariant) matrix product states with periodic boundary conditions, and systematically derive families of equations using properties of the trace algebra.

evidence.quote: Problem 20. Study the geometry of the variety of uniform matrix product states. In particular, use the properties of the trace algebra to systematically determine families of equations.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix integers $d, D \geq 2$ and $n \geq 1$. For matrices $A_1, \dots, A_d \in \mathrm{Mat}_{D \times D}(\mathbb{C})$, define the uniform (translation-invariant) matrix product state with periodic boundary conditions as the tensor
$$T(A_1,\dots,A_d) \;=\; \sum_{i_1,\dots,i_n=1}^{d} \operatorname{tr}(A_{i_1} A_{i_2} \cdots A_{i_n})\, e_{i_1} \otimes e_{i_2} \otimes \cdots \otimes e_{i_n} \;\in\; (\mathbb{C}^d)^{\otimes n},$$
where $\{e_1,\dots,e_d\}$ is the standard basis of $\mathbb{C}^d$. Let $\mathrm{uMPS}_{d,D,n} \subseteq (\mathbb{C}^d)^{\otimes n}$ denote the Zariski closure of the image of the map $(A_1,\dots,A_d) \mapsto T(A_1,\dots,A_d)$, viewed as an algebraic variety.

Recall that the trace algebra is the ring of $\mathrm{GL}_D$-invariant polynomial functions on $\mathrm{Mat}_{D\times D}(\mathbb{C})^{\oplus d}$ under simultaneous conjugation, generated by traces of words in the matrices $A_1,\dots,A_d$ (by results of Procesi and Sibirskii), with relations described by the trace ideal.

Problem: Investigate the geometry of the variety $\mathrm{uMPS}_{d,D,n}$ — including its dimension, singular locus, identifiability properties, and ideal of defining equations — and develop systematic methods, based on the structure of the trace algebra and the relations among trace monomials, for producing families of polynomial equations vanishing on $\mathrm{uMPS}_{d,D,n}$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is an active research program. Partial progress has been made (e.g., Czaplinski–Michalek–Seynnaeve studied topology, defining equations, and identifiability for uMPS; earlier work by Critch–Morton connected trace algebras to MPS), but a complete description of the variety and a systematic derivation of all its defining equations via the trace algebra remains open.

status_evidence.title: Uniform matrix product states from an algebraic geometer's point of view
status_evidence.snippet: Methods from algebraic geometry are applied to study uniform matrix product states; main results concern topology of the locus of uMPS tensors, defining equations and identifiability.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results on the geometry and defining equations of the uMPS variety exist, but the program is not complete.

status_evidence.title: Algebraic Geometry of Matrix Product States
status_evidence.snippet: Critch and Morton used trace algebras to study MPS varieties, relating them to hidden Markov models.
status_evidence.claim: Trace-algebra approach to MPS has been initiated, motivating the systematic equations program.
